title: Add Bold Tag in String
statement: You get a string `s` and a list of strings `words`. Every character of `s` that lies inside some occurrence of some word from `words` (occurrences may overlap) has to be shown in bold. Return `s` with the tags `` and `` inserted so that each maximal block of consecutive bold characters is wrapped by exactly one pair of tags: overlapping occurrences, and occurrences that end right where another begins, share a single pair. Characters outside every occurrence are left unchanged and untagged. Matching is case-sensitive.
constraints: s and words[i] consist of English letters and digits
All strings in words are distinct
notes: ## Intuition Each occurrence of a word is an interval of positions in `s`, and the tags must surround the union of those intervals, with touching intervals glued together. So the task splits into two parts: find every occurrence (string matching), then merge the intervals and print. The brute force tests every substring of `s` against a set of the words, which is O(n³) because of the slicing. ## Approach 1. For each `word`, scan `s` with `indexOf`, restarting one position after each hit so overlapping occurrences are found too. 2. For each occurrence starting at `start`, record in `reach[start]` the furthest end any word starting there reaches. 3. Sweep left to right keeping `end`, the furthest end of any interval started so far. Position `i` is bold exactly when `i < end`; this merges overlapping and touching intervals for free. 4. Build the answer: open `` where a bold run begins, copy the character, and close `` where the run ends. ## Example 1, step by step `s = "abcxyz123"`. `"abc"` occurs at 0, so `reach[0] = 3`; `"123"` occurs at 6, so `reach[6] = 9`. The sweep keeps `end = 3` for positions 0 to 5, so 0, 1, 2 are bold and 3, 4, 5 are not; at 6 `end` becomes 9, so 6, 7, 8 are bold. The output is `"abcxyz123"`. ## Complexity - Time: O(W · n · m) in the worst case, for W words of length up to m: each `indexOf` call is O(n · m) at worst; the sweep and the output are O(n). - Space: O(n) for `reach`, `bold` and `parts`. ## Pitfalls - Restart the search at `start + 1`, not `start + word.length`, or overlapping occurrences such as `"zz"` in `"zzzzz"` are missed. - Runs that only touch must share one tag pair; testing `i < end` per position handles that, while closing at each interval's end does not. - Keep the largest end per start: two words may start at the same position. - With no words, or no matches, return `s` unchanged. ## Variables | Name | Meaning | |---|---| | `n` | length of `s` | | `reach` | `reach[i]` is the furthest end of an occurrence starting at `i` (0 if none) | | `start` | position of the current occurrence of `word` | | `bold` | whether each character must be bold | | `end` | furthest end of any occurrence started at or before `i` | | `parts` | pieces of the answer, joined at the end |

narration.3: reach[i] will hold the furthest end of any word occurrence that starts at i.

narration.5: Find the first place where this word appears.
narration.6: Keep going while another occurrence was found.
narration.7: This occurrence covers start up to start + word.length; keep the longest one starting here.
narration.8: Search again from the next position, so overlapping occurrences are found too.

narration.16: Position i is bold exactly when some earlier or current occurrence still covers it.
